title: Shadow-split evaluation harness for prefetch & microbatch recommendation observability
creator: Nina Patel
description: Build an observability + experimentation harness that runs lightweight shadow-splits and small A/B cohorts to evaluate prefetch (KV prefetch/prefix cache priming) and microbatching recommendations produced by the Recommender. Goal is to quantify cost (token/GPU) vs. latency and generation-quality impact, provide statistically sound analyses, and enable an automated safe-apply / fast rollback flow for config changes.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-split traffic mode that duplicates live requests to candidate config without impacting production responses
Cohort assignment service with deterministic hashing and ability to set stratified splits per customer/route
Telemetry pipeline producing per-request: cohort_id, model_variant, tokens_generated, gpu_ms, tail_latency_ms, success_flag, quality_score_stub
Dashboard with cost vs. latency vs. quality tradeoff panels and cohort comparison widgets
Automated gating rules: non-inferiority on quality (delta <= 1.5% absolute), latency p95 within SLA, and cost reduction >= configured threshold for auto-apply
Safe rollback orchestration invoked automatically when any gate trips during rollout
Documentation + runbook and at least one internal canary run completed with results saved to the Looker/Grafana dashboards
experiment_design: Phase 0 (offline): replay 3M historical requests through candidate configs in the traffic-replay sandbox to estimate expected delta and variance
Phase 1 (shadow): 100% duplication of live traffic to candidates, observed-only for 72h, compute metrics by cohort and route
Phase 2 (stratified A/B): enable 5% traffic per cohort with stratification on prompt length bucket and customer tier for 7 days
Phase 3 (ramped rollout): staged rollout to 25/50/100% with automated safety gates and 1-hour stabilization windows
Statistical plan: sequential testing with pre-registered non-inferiority margins for quality and superiority for cost, alpha=0.05, use robust bootstrap for skewed cost distributions
primary_metrics: cost_per_completion (USD-equivalent computed from GPU-ms and token units)
model_quality_delta_percent (LLM-eval synthetic rubric + sampled human checks)
telemetry_queries: -- Grafana/SQL example: SELECT cohort, route, approx_percentile(p95_latency_ms, 0.95) as p95_latency, SUM(gpu_ms) as gpu_ms_total, SUM(tokens_generated) as tokens_total FROM inference_events WHERE timestamp BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY cohort, route;
-- Looker/BigQuery: cost_per_completion = SUM(gpu_ms * gpu_usd_per_ms + tokens_generated * token_usd) / COUNT(DISTINCT request_id)
-- Alert rule pseudo: WHEN cohort_cost_reduction < configured_threshold AND quality_delta_percent > non_inferiority_margin -> TRIP_GATE
-- Regression-adjusted estimator: use linear model controlling for prompt_length_bucket, model_variant, customer_tier to estimate treatment effect on cost_per_completion

rollout_plan: 1) Deploy harness to a non-prod replica and run traffic replay for 48h
2) Run Phase 1 shadow for 72h, validate telemetry completeness and data quality
3) Execute Phase 2 stratified A/B for 7 days; nightly checks and interim analysis at day 3
4) If gates pass, perform staged rollout 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 1-hr stabilization windows and automatic rollback on gate trip
5) Post-rollout: 14d monitoring window with automated cost/quality drift alerts
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow traffic may inflate telemetry volume and cost. Mitigation: sampling at 10% for heavy routes and run replay in isolated infra when possible.

Risk: Quality measurement is noisy for short-lived A/B trials. Mitigation: combine synthetic rubric scoring with a stratified sample of human evaluations and require non-inferiority across both metrics.
Risk: Auto-apply could regress rare edge-cases. Mitigation: require customer-tier exemptions and enable targeted exclusion lists for sensitive routes.
Risk: Race conditions in cohort assignment during canary. Mitigation: deterministic hashing and backwards-compatible cohort ids; include idempotency checks in router.
Risk: Unknown interactions with autoscaling. Mitigation: coordinate with infra on autoscaler canary config and cap burst capacity during test windows.
runbook_snippets: If Gate TRIP detected: 1) pause rollout, 2) flip feature-flag to previous config, 3) notify on-call infra and PM via #ops and PagerDuty, 4) open incident ticket and attach cohort diagnostics dashboard
Rollback checklist: record last-good-config-id, capture traces for 30 minutes post-rollback, run targeted smoke tests on top 10 routes
